mukta-m0-p62-v1526.quick_english: The eye mantra should have an anusvāra, and the weapon mantra—or, in another reading, the mantra—should be distinguished by a visarga.

mukta-m0-p62-v1527.quick_english: At the end, the priest should employ the forms joined with the appropriate class markers.

mukta-m0-p62-v1528.quick_english: Ghee, sesame seeds, barley, milk, rice grains, food offerings, and also curd are to be used.

mukta-m0-p62-v1529.quick_english: One should offer groats, flour-cake, buttermilk, and cooked rice in the daily rite.

mukta-m0-p62-v1530.quick_english: Use bilva fruit for the destruction of disease and lotus for prosperity.

mukta-m0-p62-v1531.quick_english: The five small fruits—or, in another reading, fruits—should be prepared as morsel-sized pieces of food.

mukta-m0-p62-v1532.quick_english: They should be without knots, uncracked, not crooked, and taken from the plakṣa tree.

mukta-m0-p62-v1533.quick_english: Vikaṅkata, apāmārga, and pippala indeed give peace and prosperity.

mukta-m0-p62-v1534.quick_english: In an unfavorable rite use creature hairs, and in a hatred rite use the two śigru plants described as phlegm-ending.

mukta-m0-p62-v1535.quick_english: In a killing rite, use their dust, a crow feather, and nimba blood.

mukta-m0-p62-v1536.quick_english: Śamī, dūrvā grass, and kuśa grass are oblation materials for pacifying the sun and other planets.

mukta-m0-p62-v1537.quick_english: It may be like ruby, sapphire, sunstone, pure crystal, or gold.

mukta-m0-p62-v1539.quick_english: That which is without smell, pale, dry, and resembling black charcoal is not suitable.

mukta-m0-p62-v1540.quick_english: Knowing this, the oblation in the sacrifice should be performed—or, depending on that, not performed.

mukta-m0-p62-v1541.quick_english: Likewise in the consecration-initiation and in the ablution.

mukta-m0-p62-v1542.quick_english: It should resemble a cow’s tail, be beautiful, reach a hand’s length, be without blemish, and firm.

mukta-m0-p62-v1543.quick_english: Its pit should be three fingers deep—or, in another reading, two fingers deep—with a ridge in the middle two barleycorns wide.

mukta-m0-p62-v1544.quick_english: The ladle may be made of mango, vikaṅkata, bilva, palāśa, or śiṃśapa wood.

mukta-m0-p62-v1545.quick_english: It should be six fingers in circumference, with altar height and width of eight—or, in other readings, two and eight.

mukta-m0-p62-v1546.quick_english: It should be endowed with a rim and an eight-petaled lotus, and have a capacity measuring one kuḍava.

mukta-m0-p62-v1547.quick_english: It should measure two fingers at the tip and resemble an elephant’s lip.

mukta-m0-p62-v1548.quick_english: It should be thick like the little finger, so that the ghee can flow out.

mukta-m0-p62-v1549.quick_english: At the tip of the handle, four fingers away, there should be a small platform.

mukta-m0-p62-v1550.quick_english: Having heated those two with kuśa grass, one should touch them in order from the root to the middle to the tip.

mukta-m0-p62-v1526.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p62-v1526.question: How should the eye and weapon mantras be marked by nasal or visarga?

uncertainties: Exact syntactic relation of the variant reading kh: mantraṃ is compressed.

mukta-m0-p62-v1527.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p62-v1527.question: Who must employ the class-marked forms at the end of the mantras?

These forms are to be applied at the end.

mukta-m0-p62-v1527.inference: The priest must employ the class-marked forms at the end of the mantras.
uncertainties: The precise referent of jāti in this ritual context is not fully specified.

mukta-m0-p62-v1528.question: Which substances are included among the offerings listed for ritual use?

mukta-m0-p62-v1529.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p62-v1529.question: What additional substances should be offered in the daily ritual?
premises: Groats, flour-cake, buttermilk, and cooked rice are named.
These are to be offered as oblations.

mukta-m0-p62-v1529.inference: These substances should be offered in the daily ritual.
uncertainties: The compound piṣyāka-takra-annaṃ is treated as a sequence of items in context.

mukta-m0-p62-v1530.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p62-v1530.question: Which offerings are prescribed for destroying disease and gaining prosperity?
premises: Bilva fruit is linked to the destruction of disease.
Lotus is linked to prosperity.
Both purposes are stated together.
mukta-m0-p62-v1530.inference: Bilva fruit should be used for removing disease and lotus for prosperity.

mukta-m0-p62-v1531.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p62-v1531.question: How should the five small fruits or food portions be prepared for offering?
premises: Five fruits or, in a variant, fruits are specified.
They are described as small.
They are to be taken as morsel-sized pieces of food.
mukta-m0-p62-v1531.inference: The small fruits or food items should be prepared in morsel-sized pieces.
uncertainties: The relation between paṃcaphalāni and annānāṃ is somewhat compressed.

mukta-m0-p62-v1532.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p62-v1532.question: What qualities must the sticks from the plakṣa tree possess for ritual use?
premises: The sticks must be without knots.
The sticks must be uncracked.
The sticks must be straight and come from the plakṣa tree.
mukta-m0-p62-v1532.inference: Only straight, uncracked, knotless sticks from the plakṣa tree are suitable.

mukta-m0-p62-v1533.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p62-v1533.question: Which woods or plants are said to bring peace and prosperity?
premises: Vikaṅkata, apāmārga, and pippala are named.
These are presented as suitable materials.
They are said to give peace and prosperity.
mukta-m0-p62-v1533.inference: Vikaṅkata, apāmārga, and pippala are prescribed for peace and prosperity.

mukta-m0-p62-v1534.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p62-v1534.question: What materials are prescribed for unfavorable and hatred rituals?
premises: Creature hairs are specified for an unfavorable rite.
Two śigru plants are specified for a hatred rite.
The śigru plants are qualified as phlegm-ending.
mukta-m0-p62-v1534.inference: Different materials are assigned to unfavorable and hatred rituals.
uncertainties: The exact meaning of śleṣmānta as a plant qualifier is unclear.

mukta-m0-p62-v1535.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p62-v1535.question: What substances are used together in a killing ritual?
premises: Dust from the previously mentioned items is used.
A crow feather is included.
Nimba blood is prescribed in a killing rite.
mukta-m0-p62-v1535.inference: The killing rite employs their dust, a crow feather, and nimba blood.
uncertainties: The term nimbaśoṇitam may be a technical or symbolic substance name.

mukta-m0-p62-v1536.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p62-v1536.question: Which oblation materials are prescribed for pacifying the sun and other planets?
premises: Śamī, dūrvā grass, and kuśa grass are named.
These are described as oblation materials.
Their purpose is pacification of the sun and other planets.
mukta-m0-p62-v1536.inference: Śamī, dūrvā, and kuśa are oblation materials for planetary pacification.

mukta-m0-p62-v1537.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p62-v1537.question: What gem-like appearances are associated with an auspicious quality?
premises: Appearances like ruby, sapphire, sunstone, and pure crystal are listed.
An appearance like gold is also listed.
These comparisons describe a desirable quality.
mukta-m0-p62-v1537.inference: Auspicious material may resemble ruby, sapphire, sunstone, pure crystal, or gold.

mukta-m0-p62-v1538.question: What evaluative quality applies to the previously described appearances?
premises: The previous verse listed desirable appearances.
This verse gives a single evaluative term.

mukta-m0-p62-v1539.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p62-v1539.question: What characteristics mark an item as unsuitable in contrast to the auspicious type?

Resembling black charcoal is listed.

mukta-m0-p62-v1539.inference: An item with these characteristics is unsuitable.

mukta-m0-p62-v1541.inference: The same rule applies in consecration-initiation and in ablution.

mukta-m0-p62-v1544.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
